'''Liu Yandong''' ({{lang-zh|c=刘延东}}; November 22, 1945 – October 28, 2026) was a Chinese politician. She served as a [[Vice Premier of China|vice premier of the PRC]] from 2013 to 2018, and was a member of the [[Politburo of the Chinese Communist Party]] from 2007 to 2017, a [[State Councilor]] between 2007 and 2012, and was [[head of the United Front Work Department]] of the Communist Party between 2002 and 2007.

Liu was a graduate of [[Tsinghua University]], and was associated throughout her career with her fellow alumnus and [[Communist Youth League of China|Communist Youth League]] colleague [[Hu Jintao]]. As such Chinese-language media has sometimes labelled Liu as part of the so-called "''[[Tuanpai]]''", or "Youth League clique". After the retirement of Vice Premier [[Wu Yi (politician)|Wu Yi]], Liu became the highest-ranked female political figure in China, and one of only three women to have held a seat on the Politburo since 1987, the others being Wu and retired Vice Premier [[Sun Chunlan]].{{efn|Prior to 1987, female Politburo members, such as [[Ye Qun]], [[Deng Yingchao]], and [[Jiang Qing]], were invariably wives of party leaders.}}<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/oct/16/china-liu-yandong-feminism-politics|title=China's Liu Yandong carries the hopes – and fears – of modern feminism|author-first1=Tania |author-last1=Branigan|work=The Guardian|date=October 16, 2012 }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Liu was born on November 22,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ruan |first1=Yulin |title=刘延东纽约阐释“中国梦”：通过和平发展方式实现 |url=https://www.chinanews.com.cn/gn/2013/11-23/5538183.shtml |access-date=October 29, 2026 |work=www.chinanews.com.cn |date=November 22, 2013 |quote=中新社纽约11月22日电 (记者 阮煜琳)“我很高兴在纽约——我访美即将结束的最后一站，能和在座的朋友们共同度过我的生日。一般过生日都是与家人在一起，但今天我在纽约与各位朋友在一起，就像和我的家人一样，度过我非常愉快的生日……” 中国国务院副总理刘延东22日出席纽约卡内基音乐厅招待酒会时开诚布公地对大家说。 [　NEW YORK, Nov. 22 (China News Service reporter Ruan Yulin) -- "I am very happy to spend my birthday with you all in New York—the last stop of my visit to the United States. Usually, birthdays are spent with family, but today in New York with you all feels like being with my own family, and I am having a very enjoyable birthday..." Chinese Vice Premier Liu Yandong said candidly at a reception at Carnegie Hall in New York on November 22.]|language=zh}}</ref> 1945 in [[Nantong|Nantong County]], [[Jiangsu]].<ref name="Xinhua2012">{{cite news |title=Liu Yandong – Member of Political Bureau of CPC Central Committee |url=http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/special/18cpcnc/2012-11/15/c_131977294.htm |work=Xinhua |date=November 15, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121120090225/http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/special/18cpcnc/2012-11/15/c_131977294.htm |archive-date=November 20, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Olympedia">{{cite web |title=Liu Yandong |url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/1200890 |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=October 28, 2026}}</ref><ref name="DNA">{{cite news |title=Liu Yandong: The woman who charmed China |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/world/report-liu-yandong-the-woman-who-charmed-china-1812270 |work=[[DNA India]] |access-date=October 28, 2026}}</ref> Her father, Liu Ruilong, was a communist organiser who served as party secretary of Nantong County in the late 1920s, and he later became a vice-minister of agriculture.<ref name="RMZXW2024">{{cite news |url=https://www.rmzxw.com.cn/c/2024-02-23/3495280.shtml |script-title=zh:何昆和红十四军的创建 |trans-title=He Kun and the Founding of the 14th Red Army |work=CPPCC Daily Online |date=February 23, 2024 |access-date=October 28, 2026 |language=zh}}</ref><ref name="CMP2007">{{cite web |last=Qian |first=Gang |translator-last=Bandurski |translator-first=David |title=Power factions, "princelings" and political pasts |url=https://chinamediaproject.org/2007/09/14/power-factions-princelings-and-political-pasts/ |website=China Media Project |date=September 14, 2007 |access-date=October 28, 2026}}</ref><ref name="BBC2012">{{cite news |title=China's congress: Front-runners for power |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-19703672 |work=[[BBC News]] |date=September 24, 2012 |access-date=October 28, 2026}}</ref> Because of her father's revolutionary background, some analysts have classified her as a [[princeling]].<ref name="Telegraph">{{cite news |last=Moore |first=Malcolm |title=Demise of Bo Xilai paves way for Liu Yandong, China's most powerful woman |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/asia/china/9198599/Demise-of-Bo-Xilai-paves-way-for-Liu-Yandong-Chinas-most-powerful-woman.html |work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=April 11, 2012 |access-date=October 28, 2026}}</ref><ref name="BBC2012" />
 
She joined the [[Chinese Communist Party]] in July 1964.<ref name="People2012">{{cite news |url=https://cpc.people.com.cn/18/BIG5/n/2012/1115/c350821-19594786.html |script-title=zh:刘延东简历 |trans-title=Résumé of Liu Yandong |work=People's Daily Online |date=November 15, 2012 |access-date=October 28, 2026 |language=zh}}</ref> From 1964 to 1970, she studied in the Department of Engineering Chemistry at Tsinghua University, where she also served as a political counsellor for her year group.<ref name="People2012" /><ref name="BJNews2013">{{cite news |url=https://m.bjnews.com.cn/detail/155146126414126.html |script-title=zh:刘延东简历 |trans-title=Résumé of Liu Yandong |work=The Beijing News |date=March 17, 2013 |access-date=October 28, 2026 |language=zh}}</ref> While working, she later earned a master's degree in sociology from [[Renmin University of China]], from 1990 to 1994, and a doctorate in law, in political theory, from the School of Administration of [[Jilin University]], from 1994 to 1998.<ref name="BJNews2013" /><ref name="People2012" />

==Early career==
After graduating, Liu began work in March 1970 at the Kaiping Chemical Plant in [[Tangshan]], [[Hebei]], where she rose from worker to technician and head of a [[polysilicon]] workshop.<ref name="People2012" /><ref name="Telegraph" /> From 1972 to 1980, she worked at the Beijing Chemical Experimental Plant, where she held posts including head of the political department and, from 1978, deputy party secretary.<ref name="People2012" /> In 1980, she moved to the organisation department of the Beijing Municipal Party Committee, and from 1981 to 1982, she was deputy party secretary of [[Chaoyang District, Beijing|Chaoyang District]].<ref name="People2012" />
 
From 1982 to 1991, Liu was a secretary and later executive secretary of the Secretariat of the Communist Youth League Central Committee, and she was successively vice-chair and chair of the [[All-China Youth Federation]].<ref name="People2012" /><ref name="BJNews2013" /> In the Youth League, she worked as a deputy to Hu Jintao, who, like her, was a Tsinghua graduate.<ref name="BBC2012" /> She was also a member of the Standing Committee of the 7th [[National People's Congress]].<ref name="People2012" />

==United Front Work Department==
In 1991, Liu joined the [[United Front Work Department]] as deputy secretary-general and then deputy head, while remaining chair of the All-China Youth Federation until 1995.<ref name="People2012" /> From 1995, she was also party secretary of the [[Central Institute of Socialism]], and in 2001, she was given full ministerial rank.<ref name="People2012" /> In 2002, she became head of the department, a post she held until 2007.<ref name="People2012" /> In 2003, she was also elected a vice-chair of the 10th National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference.<ref name="People2012" /><ref name="Xinhua2026">{{cite news |url=https://www.news.cn/20261028/fa8dfbdf4b874dd2a96c6b51a1ce5f35/c.html |script-title=zh:刘延东同志逝世 |trans-title=Comrade Liu Yandong Dies |work=Xinhua News Agency |date=October 28, 2026 |access-date=October 28, 2026 |language=zh}}</ref>
 
==Politburo and State Council==
===State councilor===
[[File:Visita de Consejera de Estado de Gobierno de China, Liu Yandong (5297030111).jpg|thumb|Liu at the [[Palacio de Carondelet]] in Ecuador (2010)]]
At the [[17th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party|17th Party Congress]] in 2007, Liu was elected to the Politburo.<ref name="People2012" /> In March 2008, she became a state councilor and a member of the party group of the [[State Council of China|State Council]], and she was also a vice-president of the [[Beijing Organizing Committee for the Olympic Games]].<ref name="People2012" /><ref name="Olympedia" /> In 2008, she received the [[Olympic Order]] in silver and the [[Paralympic Order]].<ref name="Olympedia" /><ref name="IPC2008">{{cite press release |title=Paralympic Order Recipients 2008 Honoured |url=https://www.paralympic.org/index%2Ephp/es/node/78070 |publisher=[[International Paralympic Committee]] |date=October 23, 2008 |access-date=October 28, 2026}}</ref> In 2009, [[Stony Brook University]] awarded her an honorary doctorate, and New York state senator [[Toby Ann Stavisky]] who attended the ceremony described her as the highest-ranking woman in the Chinese government.<ref name="NYSenate2009">{{cite web |last=Stavisky |first=Toby Ann |author-link=Toby Ann Stavisky |title=Sen. Stavisky attends honorary doctorate ceremony at SUNY Stony Brook |url=https://www.nysenate.gov/newsroom/articles/2009/toby-ann-stavisky/sen-stavisky-attends-honorary-doctorate-ceremony-suny |publisher=[[New York State Senate]] |date=May 1, 2009 |access-date=October 28, 2026}}</ref> By 2012, she was the only woman on the 25-member Politburo, and she was regarded as a long-shot candidate to become the first woman on its [[Politburo Standing Committee of the Chinese Communist Party|Standing Committee]].<ref name="Guardian2012">{{cite news |last=Branigan |first=Tania |title=China's Liu Yandong carries the hopes – and fears – of modern feminism |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/oct/16/china-liu-yandong-feminism-politics |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=October 16, 2012 |access-date=October 28, 2026}}</ref><ref name="BBC2012" />

===Vice premier===
[[File:Liu Yandong with Reuven Rivlin 2016 (1).jpg|thumb|Liu with the [[President of Israel]], [[Reuven Rivlin]], in March 2016]]

At the [[18th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party|18th Party Congress]] in November 2012, Liu was re-elected to the Politburo, which for the first time since the [[Cultural Revolution]] had two female members, her and [[Sun Chunlan]].<ref name="People2012" /><ref name="Brookings2017">{{cite web |last=Li |first=Cheng |author-link=Cheng Li |title=Status of China's women leaders on the eve of 19th Party Congress |url=https://www.brookings.edu/articles/status-of-chinas-women-leaders-on-the-eve-of-19th-party-congress |publisher=[[Brookings Institution]] |date=March 30, 2017 |access-date=October 28, 2026}}</ref> In March 2013, she was appointed vice premier in the government of [[Li Keqiang]].<ref name="BJNews2013" /> She was responsible for education, health, culture and sport, and she chaired the Academic Degrees Committee of the State Council.<ref name="IANS2018">{{cite news |title=Chinese Vice Premier to attend PyeongChang Olympics' closing ceremony |url=https://thequint.com/news/hot-news/chinese-vice-premier-to-attend-pyeongchang-olympics-closing-ceremony |work=[[The Quint]] |agency=[[Indo-Asian News Service]] |date=February 19, 2018 |access-date=October 28, 2026}}</ref><ref name="GovCN2013">{{cite news |url=https://www.gov.cn/ldhd/2013-07/10/content_2444406.htm |script-title=zh:刘延东：深化改革 推进研究生教育内涵式发展 |trans-title=Liu Yandong: Deepen Reform and Promote Quality-Based Development of Graduate Education |work=Central People's Government of the People's Republic of China |date=July 10, 2013 |access-date=October 28, 2026 |language=zh}}</ref> In February 2018, she attended the closing ceremony of the [[2018 Winter Olympics]] in [[Pyeongchang County|Pyeongchang]], South Korea as the envoy of Chinese leader [[Xi Jinping]], when the Games were handed over to Beijing as host of the [[2022 Winter Olympics]].<ref name="IANS2018" /> In May 2017, she was awarded the Russian [[Order of Friendship]] in recognition of her significant contribution to 'strengthening cooperation with the [[Russian Federation]].'<ref>{{cite web|url=http://kremlin.ru/acts/bank/41943|title=Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 25.05.2017 г. № 238|trans-title=Decree of the President of the Russian Federation of May 25, 2017 No. 238|lang=ru|newspaper=President of Russia|date=May 25, 2017|access-date=October 29, 2026}}</ref>
 
Liu retired from the Politburo at the [[19th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party|19th Party Congress]] in October 2017, leaving Sun Chunlan as its only female member.<ref name="QZ2017">{{cite news |title=And then there was one: A lone female sits among the top of China's Communist Party |url=https://qz.com/1107385/china-female-politician-a-lone-female-sun-chunlan-sits-at-the-top-of-chinas-communist-party |work=[[Quartz (publication)|Quartz]] |date=October 25, 2017 |access-date=October 28, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Brookings2017" /> Her term as vice premier ended on March 19, 2018, when the National People's Congress endorsed [[Han Zheng]], Sun Chunlan, [[Hu Chunhua]] and [[Liu He (politician)|Liu He]] as vice premiers.<ref name="CD2018">{{cite news |title=China's new cabinet members endorsed |url=https://govt.chinadaily.com.cn/s/201803/19/WS5c9f09ad498e079e6801c880/chinas-new-cabinet-members-endorsed.html |work=[[China Daily]] |date=March 19, 2018 |access-date=October 28, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Liu was married for more than 40 years to Yang Yuanxing, who ran his own technology company, and the couple had one daughter.<ref name="BBC2012" /> Liu died in Beijing on October 28, 2026, at the age of 80.<ref name="Xinhua2026" /><ref name="Reuters2026">{{cite news |title=China's former Vice Premier Liu Yandong has died, Xinhua says |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/china/chinas-former-vice-premier-liu-yandong-has-died-xinhua-says-2026-10-28/ |publisher=[[Reuters]] |date=October 28, 2026 |access-date=October 28, 2026}}</ref>
